context_heading: What to understand about licensed conveyancers and local search
context: Licensed conveyancers are regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers and are qualified to handle purchases, sales and remortgages. They must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow strict rules on handling client money. You can check that a conveyancer is licensed by looking on the Council for Licensed Conveyancers register.

Many lenders only work with conveyancers on their panel, and the Law Society's Conveyancing Quality Scheme is a common accreditation. Before you instruct a local conveyancer, check that they are on your lender's panel if you are buying with a mortgage. It also helps to ask about their experience with the type of property you are dealing with.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us whether you are buying, selling or remortgaging, and whether the property is freehold or leasehold.
Let us know the approximate location of the property so we can introduce you to a conveyancer near you.
Mention if you have a deadline, such as a mortgage offer expiry or a planned move date.
Say whether your lender has a panel of conveyancers and whether you need someone on that panel.
Include any specific concerns, such as a leasehold property, a shared ownership scheme or a new build.
Tell us if you have already started the process with another conveyancer and are looking to switch.
questions: Are you regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers, and what is your registration number?
Are you on my lender's panel of approved conveyancers?
What are your fees and what do they include, and are there any additional costs such as disbursements?
How will you keep me updated on progress, and who will be my main point of contact?
Do you have experience with the type of property I am buying or selling, such as leasehold or new build?
What is your process for handling client money, and which bank account will my deposit be held in?

faqs.a: A licensed conveyancer is a property law specialist regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. They are qualified to handle purchases, sales and remortgages, and must follow strict rules on handling client money.

faqs.q: How do I check that a conveyancer is licensed?
faqs.a: You can check the Council for Licensed Conveyancers register, which lists all licensed conveyancers and firms. It is a good idea to do this before you instruct anyone.

faqs.q: Do I need a conveyancer on my lender's panel?
faqs.a: Many lenders only work with conveyancers on their panel, so it is important to check this before you instruct a conveyancer. If your chosen conveyancer is not on the panel, your lender may not accept them.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a licensed conveyancer near me?
faqs.a: We introduce you to a suitable UK professional based on what you tell us, and they will quote you directly. We do not provide the service ourselves and are not regulated, so you should satisfy yourself that the conveyancer is right for you.
